background: NatWest Group is the holding company of the UK's largest business bank, owner of NatWest, Royal Bank of Scotland, Ulster Bank and Coutts, returned to full private ownership after its financial-crisis rescue.
synthesis: All three of the main agencies rate the group, A on average and A- at the weakest of them, all three on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 10 Sep 2025. Capital is on the weak side of the UK majors, CET1 of 13.2% in the bottom quarter and leverage of 4.7% below the peer median, which is where the attention belongs. Liquidity is unremarkable, LCR of 140% below the peer median and down 10 points since 30 Jun 2025, NSFR of 132% above it, with CET1 and leverage broadly flat over the same span (figures to 30 Jun 2026). Everything flagged in the last 90 days is favourable, a strong first half and raised guidance reported through July and into 18 Sep 2026.
